messages:
emily.k: kicking off a staged rollout for api-gateway v3.2.0 -> starting at 5% traffic in eu-west. gonna watch p95 and error-rate for 15m then 25% if green. deploy details in the doc: https://redwood.internal/deploys/3.2.0

deploy-bot: promote request received. plan: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 15m observation windows. Rollback on >=1.0% 5xx or latency p95 > 600ms for two consecutive windows.

rafal: noted. oncall is paged and watching. can we pin legacy-model to avoid cross-variant policy mismatch?

emily.k: good call — pinning legacy-model v1.9.4 for eu-west routing group for duration of rollout.

ben: heads up — I saw a brief spike on a previous canary when kvcache warmed. let's enable warm-cache flag in canary only to reduce noise.

emily.k: enabling warm-cache for canary. command I'll run:
```
deployctl set-flag --service api-gateway --env eu-west --flag warm_cache=true --scope canary
```

sara: quick question — if we hit the error threshold, do we auto-rollback or stop and wait for manual? what's our handoff?

emily.k: for this rollout we set stop-and-escalate. deploy-bot will pause and post a hold call in this thread. oncall then decides rollback vs mitigation.

oncall-bot: oncall rota: rafal (primary), maria (secondary). Paging rafal now.

rafal: I'm in. watching dashboards (canary: eu-west). setting alerts for 5xx and p95 > 600ms.

deploy-bot: canary at 5% now. traffic split: 95/5.

maria: tagging perf reviewer @maria for visibility. please flag any regressions in the next 15m.

ben: seeing a small error cluster around /auth callback at +3m, 0.15% 5xx. still under threshold but keep eyes.

emily.k: observed same. stack traces look like oauth token validation timeout from upstream idp. pinging platform team.

platform-bridge (message relayed): platform team investigating auth idp latency, might be transient. recommend hold if 5xx crosses 1.0%

rafal: agree, hold if it increases. current metrics: 5xx 0.22%, p95 420ms.

(10m into canary)

emily.k: metrics look stable. preparing to move to 25% in 5.

deploy-bot: rolling to 25% now. note: when we increase to 25% warm-cache flag will remain enabled for canary only.

ben: after bump, keep an eye on cold-start latencies for newly routed instances.

(3m after bump)

both: spike — 5xx jumped to 1.3% for ~2m window, auth callback errors up.

oncall-bot: threshold breached: 5xx >= 1.0%. Pausing rollout.

emily.k: pausing. holding at 25%. collecting logs. would recommend rollback if errors don't drop below 0.5% within 10m.

maria: attaching quick repro snippet from logs:
```
ERROR oauth: token validation timeout id=abcd user=x
trace: grpc: deadline exceeded
```

rafal: mitigation idea — temporarily divert auth calls to fallback token-issuer region via routing rule. can be toggled quickly but requires config push. thoughts?

ben: that might mask issue but buys time. if we do config flip, we should also reduce canary to 5% again to reduce blast radius.

emily.k: agree. options: 1) rollback to v3.1.9 now (fast) 2) route auth to fallback region + scale idp proxy (medium) 3) wait 10m (risky). My vote is rollback to minimize customer impact.

rafal: +1 rollback. I'm ready to execute and monitor.

maria: +1 rollback from SRE side. will coordinate change window if needed.

ben: ok. executing rollback runbook. command: 
```
deployctl promote --service api-gateway --version v3.1.9 --percent 100 --reason "canary auth 5xx spike"
```

deploy-bot: rollback initiated by ben. estimated time to full traffic: ~4m. posting CI links and release notes diff.

emily.k: thanks team. I'll open a follow-up postmortem and add a prompt-eval to catch auth-related regressions in preflight.

rafal: monitoring now. current 5xx decreasing to 0.2% as rollback proceeds.

deploy-bot: rollback complete. traffic at 100% v3.1.9.

emily.k: filing incident ticket and flagging for postmortem: INC-2026-042. tagging product and platform for root-cause follow-up. :white_check_mark:

maria: nice fast ops. leaving notes in the runbook to consider auto-reduce to 5% on routing fixes next time rather than full rollback.

ben: agree. closing thread after postmortem created. thanks all. :thumbsup:
